rounds.text: Cyber Media Research & Services Ltd trades at a remarkably low price-to-earnings ratio of 4.65 and a price-to-book ratio of 0.91, alongside a healthy dividend yield of 3.15% [E1, E2, E4]. This cheap valuation is paired with robust financial health and profitability, demonstrated by a 22.0% ROCE, a 19.6% ROE, and conservatively managed borrowings of Rs 5 Cr with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.25 [E6, E7, E27, E28]. Growth metrics further highlight the disconnect between price and fundamental performance, with 5-year compounded sales growth at 25% and profit growth at 41%, while trailing twelve-month sales and profits surged by 46% and 45% respectively [E8, E10, E11, E13]. Independent valuation models reinforce this mispricing, indicating an intrinsic value pointing to a substantial margin of safety, with the current share price implying a negative 13.1% growth rate against management's baseline expectations [E33, E34, E35]. Management continues to drive momentum by outpacing industry growth, adding over 50 logos in digital marketing, securing new clients in D2C and education, and targeting up to 100 logos for CMGalaxy [E64, E67, E74, E75]. Conceded: operating margins have seen a slight compression down to 5% in the TTM alongside inconsistent trends, and cash conversion remains weak with operating cash flow at only 38% of operating profit [E19, E21, E23, E26].

Conceded: the company trades at a low P/E of 4.65 and price-to-book of 0.91 [E1, E2]. However, this low valuation reflects profound operational degradation and market rejection, as evidenced by a share price sitting deep at 18% to 25% of its 52-week range and lagging the market with a relative-strength rating of 0 [E5, E36, E39]. Operating margins have compressed to 5% in the trailing twelve months down from 7% three years earlier, and quarterly margins remain inconsistent [E19, E21]. Despite reported profit growth, cash generation is alarming: operating cash flow for March 2026 was a mere 38% of operating profit with a cash conversion ratio of 0.33x, leaving free cash flow at negative zero [E23, E25, E26]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is evaporating, with foreign institutional holdings dropping to 0.93% from 3.77%, and the international segment facing flat growth compounded by negative dollar impacts [E31, E79].
